```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

In multi-label classification, each observation can be associated with several
labels at once. CCNR fits a classifier chain network, in which every label
receives the predictions of the labels before it in the chain, and the
parameters of all labels are estimated jointly. This vignette walks through a
complete analysis: fitting a model, choosing the label order, selecting the
tuning parameters by cross-validation, evaluating predictions on held-out data,
and inspecting the estimated label interdependencies. The method itself is
described in Touw and Van de Velden (2025).

## Data

The `amphibians` data set records the presence of seven amphibian species at
189 water reservoirs in Poland. The site characteristics are summarized by 25
principal components, which serve as the explanatory variables.

```{r}
library(CCNR)
data(amphibians)
X <- amphibians$X
Y <- amphibians$Y
dim(X)
round(colMeans(Y), 2)
```

The species differ considerably in prevalence. The great crested newt
(`CrestNewt`) is present at only 11% of the sites.

To evaluate the final model on data it has not seen, 140 sites are used for
training and the remaining 49 are set aside.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
train <- sample(nrow(X), 140)
X_train <- X[train, ]
Y_train <- Y[train, ]
X_test  <- X[-train, ]
Y_test  <- Y[-train, ]
```

## Fitting a model

`ccn` takes the explanatory variables `x`, the binary label matrix `y`, and two
tuning parameters: `q`, which controls how the losses of the labels are
aggregated, and the ridge penalty `lambda`.

```{r}
model <- ccn(X_train, Y_train, q = 1.5, lambda = 0.5)
model
```

`summary` prints the estimated intercepts `b`, the coefficients `W` of the
explanatory variables, and the coefficients `C` of the label predictions. The
coefficients of the principal components are of little interest here, so `W`
is left out.

```{r}
summary(model, which = c("b", "C"))
```

The same estimates are returned as a list by `coef`. The methods `fitted` and
`residuals` are also available.

## Choosing the label order

The order of the labels in the chain determines which labels can inform which.
By default, the column order of `y` is used. `entropy_label_order` derives an
order from the labels themselves.

```{r}
colnames(Y_train)[entropy_label_order(Y_train, method = "cebcc1")]
```

The `label_order` argument of `ccn` accepts either such a permutation or a
function of `x` and `y` that returns one. A function is evaluated on the data
that are actually used for fitting, which matters during cross-validation:
the order is then recomputed on every set of training folds.

```{r}
cebcc1_order <- function(x, y) entropy_label_order(y, method = "cebcc1")
```

## Selecting the tuning parameters

With rare labels, a random split into folds can leave a label without any
positive examples in some fold. `multilabel_stratified_folds` assigns the
observations to folds such that the proportion of every label stays close to
its proportion in the full data.

```{r}
fold_id <- multilabel_stratified_folds(Y_train, folds = 5, seed = 1)
round(t(sapply(1:5, function(k) colMeans(Y_train[fold_id == k, ]))), 2)
```

`ccn_cv` evaluates every combination of the candidate values for `q`,
`lambda`, and `label_order`. Candidate label orders are given as a named list,
in which `NULL` stands for the column order of `y`. By default, combinations
are scored with the Hamming accuracy.

```{r}
cv <- ccn_cv(X_train, Y_train, q = c(1, 2), lambda = c(0.1, 0.5, 1),
             label_order = list(default = NULL, cebcc1 = cebcc1_order),
             fold_assignments = fold_id)
cv$best_params
```

The selected model, refitted on all training data, is available as
`cv$best_model`. The methods `predict`, `coef`, `fitted`, and `residuals` can
also be applied to `cv` directly.

## Prediction and evaluation

`predict` returns predicted labels by default and predicted probabilities for
`type = "response"`. Labels are obtained by comparing the probabilities with a
threshold of 0.5. A vector of thresholds, one per label, can be supplied
instead. Setting each threshold to the prevalence of the label in the training
data helps to detect rare labels.

```{r}
Y_prob  <- predict(cv, newdata = X_test, type = "response")
Y_class <- predict(cv, newdata = X_test)
Y_class_prev <- predict(cv, newdata = X_test, threshold = colMeans(Y_train))
```

The package provides scoring functions for multi-label predictions. Those
based on predicted labels depend on the threshold, while the log-likelihood
and the mean area under the ROC curve use the probabilities.

```{r}
predictions <- list(threshold_0.5 = Y_class, prevalence = Y_class_prev)
round(sapply(predictions, function(p) c(
    hamming     = ccn_hamming_accuracy(Y_test, p),
    exact_match = ccn_exact_match(Y_test, p),
    micro_f1    = ccn_micro_f1(Y_test, p),
    macro_f1    = ccn_macro_f1(Y_test, p))), 3)

ccn_log_likelihood(Y_test, Y_prob)
ccn_mean_auc(Y_test, Y_prob)
```

Any of these, or a function of your own, can be passed to the `scoring`
argument of `ccn_cv`. A scoring function receives the arguments `y_true`,
`y_class`, and `y_prob` and returns a single number, where larger is better.

## Label interdependencies

The matrix `C` contains the estimated effect of the prediction for one label
on the prediction for another. Rows correspond to the predicted label and
columns to the labels that precede it in the chain, so the matrix is lower
triangular.

```{r}
round(coef(cv)$C, 3)
```

A positive entry means that a higher predicted presence of the earlier species
increases the predicted presence of the later one, after accounting for the
site characteristics. Because `C` is penalized together with `W`, the size of
the entries depends on `lambda`.

## Further reading

The help pages of the functions used here contain further options and
examples. `generate_dataset` creates a small synthetic data set that is
convenient for experimenting with the package.

## Reference

Touw, D. J. W. and Van de Velden, M. (2025). Classifier chain networks for
multi-label classification. *Expert Systems with Applications*, 286, 128048.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2025.128048>
